_about: The first scheme that opens on the road rather than in a town, and the only use of
the `invitation` and `kin` carriers — the two that reach a person rather than a
place. An invitation is the one piece of news in the vocabulary that is *addressed*
to the player and expects an answer, which is why it took a scheme about being
asked to somebody's house to use it.
It is also the only scheme with no antagonist at all. Nothing here is a crime, a
debt, a beast or a lie; it is a family deciding something and a stranger being
asked to say what they think. Eleven of the twelve schemes before it turn on
somebody wanting something they should not have.
Both endings are kind. The scheme's whole question is whether the player takes a
side in a house that is not theirs, and it is the rare one where refusing is not
a failure and not a shrug — the household closes ranks and thinks better of you.

schemes.title: An invitation
schemes.about: A household asks a stranger to a gathering, because a stranger owes nobody there anything.

cards.title: $elder's gathering at $lodging
objectives: Go to $lodging when the day comes
Say what you think, or do not
cards.reward: a seat at the table, and whatever that turns out to be worth

cards.title: What $elder is really asking
facts: $elder means to pass the house to $heir and knows the rest of the household will not have it said by anyone who lives in it.
$heir does not want it and has not found a way to say so in front of $elder.

grants_on_open.say: the invitation named a day and a house and no occasion at all

action.says: $elder asks you to $lodging on a named day, and does not say what for.

tell.silent: The invitation from $elder is on its way out to $road.

tell.perceptible: $heir is at $market and would rather talk about anything but $elder's house.

action.text: $elder wants it said out loud by somebody the household owes nothing to, which is why the invitation went to a stranger on $road.

tell.perceptible: $elder wanted a stranger to say it, and says so without embarrassment.

also.says: $elder's household has settled what it was going to argue about, and a stranger was there for it.

tell.perceptible: It gets said at $lodging, and the room takes it better from you than it would have from $heir.
You eat at $elder's table and say nothing about the house, and nobody presses.
